subject: OEM quote: lead-time windows & partial allocation plan for ACME
messages:
From: Timothy Scott <timothy.scott@oemvendor.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme.ai
Date: Thu, 24 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: OEM quote and lead-time assumptions for ACME deal

Alex — attaching our initial quote and lead-time assumptions for the ACME allocation (oem_quote_Q3.pdf). High level: 200 A100x2 equivalent nodes, split-shipment allowed in 3 waves. Current lead-time window: 12–18 weeks from PO for full build; partial allocations available in 6–9 weeks for early-batch fulfillment.

Key assumptions in the PDF: OEM testing/firmware validation is included in lead times; any firmware customization or locked BIOS will add 2–4 weeks. Freight to your preferred US sites is quoted separately.

Quick ask: can you confirm the committed PO date window (we penciled 2026-10-15 to 2026-10-22) and whether you need staggered delivery (we can hold 30% for a later slot).

Thanks,
Timothy Scott
Account Director — OEM Sales
Omega Systems Inc.
Attachment: oem_quote_Q3.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)

---
From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
To: Timothy Scott <timothy.scott@oemvendor.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, procurement@acme.ai
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OEM quote and lead-time assumptions for ACME deal

Tim — thanks for the PDF and the timing guidance. A few clarifications from our side to help scope the PO and our Dedicated capacity plan: 

1) Ramp profile: ACME expects a soft launch Nov 29 with production load by Jan 15. That means we need at least 40% of capacity in region-us-west by mid-November and 100% by mid-January.
2) Staggered deliveries: we prefer 3-wave deliveries but need the second wave no later than 2026-12-15. Can you confirm you can guarantee the second wave window or offer substitution (equivalent SKUs) if primary SKUs slip?
3) Partial acceptance & testing: we will perform acceptance tests and may hold final acceptance on final wave. Please include standard test scripts and firmware/hash verification steps in the delivery checklist.
4) PO timing: we can aim for PO issuance 2026-10-20 but want to include a credit/penalty clause for >2 week slips after confirmed ETA.

Marissa — can you confirm commercial levers we can offer (holdbacks, credits) if OEM misses second-wave date?
Dev — any constraints from infra side on early-batch activation (racks, power, cooling, firmware)?

Appreciate the fast turnaround — attaching internal ramp plan for context.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Head of Sales, Dedicated Capacity
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_acme_rampplan_v1.pdf (PDF, 450KB)

---

To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Timothy Scott <timothy.scott@oemvendor.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, procurement@acme.ai
Date: Sat, 26 Sep 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OEM quote and lead-time assumptions for ACME deal

Team — brief commercial position:
- We can accept a 3-wave delivery, but contractually we need an SLA on second-wave ETA (target no later than 2026-12-15) with a liquidated-damage credit starting at day +7.
- Holdback: recommend 20% holdback on final invoice pending final acceptance testing (FAT) on final wave.
- Pricing: will confirm if we can push for a small volume discount tied to earlier payment (net-30 vs net-45).

Procurement@acme.ai — please confirm whether ACME can sign a PO with those commercial conditions. If ACME prefers cloud-side bridging vs hardware on-prem, that changes timing.

Marissa
Senior Sales Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Timothy Scott <timothy.scott@oemvendor.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 10:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OEM quote and lead-time assumptions for ACME deal

Short technical note from infra:
- SKU compatibility: we can accept A100x2 or equivalent A800 configurations. If substitution occurs, we need a BIN-level matrix and a validated kernel/driver build.
- Early-batch activation: need 5 dedicated racks cabled and powered in us-west by 2026-11-18 for initial onboarding/testing. Rack build lead time is 3–4 weeks once components arrive.
- Firmware/BIOS: any non-standard firmware requires a 2-week validation window; prefer locked/immutable images from OEM with SHA256 checksums included in shipment manifest.
- Cloud bridging: SuppliersCloud (cloudsales@supplierscloud.com) sited that they can provide temporary reserved capacity within 2 weeks but at 25% higher unit cost; pros/cons attached in a short table.

Action items:
- Timothy: confirm substitution policy and provide BIN matrix + expected firmware hashes.
- Alex/Marissa: decide whether to sign PO with holdback or secure short-term cloud bridge while OEM completes final wave.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Director, Infrastructure Operations
Redwood Inference
Attachment: infra_early_batch_requirements.txt (TXT, 4KB)

From: Timothy Scott <timothy.scott@oemvendor.com>

Alex / team — updated plan after internal capacity review and factory scheduling. Summary below and attached revised capacity schedule (capacity_schedule_v2.xlsx):

1) Commitment windows: PO received between 2026-10-15 and 2026-10-22 -> wave 1: 60–80 units_ship in 6–8 weeks (ETA early Dec), wave 2: 60–80 units_ship in 10–12 weeks (ETA mid-Dec to early Jan), final wave: remaining units by 14–18 weeks (ETA end Jan). If PO is after 2026-10-22 we move to next factory slot (+4 weeks each wave).
2) Substitutions: we will allow OEM-equivalent substitutions only with pre-approved BIN matrix and driver build validation. We will provide BIN matrix and firmware hashes by 2026-10-04.
3) Partial testing & manifests: each shipment will include firmware hashes and a signed FAT checklist.
4) Credits: Omega can accept a small contractual credit for misses beyond the 2-week buffer; we will provide formal language for your legal team by 2026-10-06.
5) PO & next steps: Please issue PO to oem_orders@omegasystems.com by 2026-10-20 to lock factory slot. Reference: PO# P-ACME-114 (provisional).

If you want to avoid a bridging cost, consider issuing PO on the 2026-10-15 window. For immediate capacity we can coordinate with SuppliersCloud for a short-term reserved bridge — let me know and I will make an introduction.

Regards,
Timothy Scott
Account Director — OEM Sales
Omega Systems Inc.
Attachment: capacity_schedule_v2.xlsx (XLSX, 120KB)
